definition: The substratum where qualities and actions reside.
details: Nine substances of existence: Earth (pṛthivī), Water (ap), Light (tejas), Wind (vāyu), Ether (ākāśa), Time (kāla), Space (dik), Self (ātman), and Mind (manas).

definition: Static, inherent features of substances that do not possess actions themselves.
details: Historically 24 qualities, including Color (rūpa), Taste (rasa), Smell (gandha), Touch (sparśa), Number (saṃkhyā), Dimension (parimāṇa), Conjunction (saṃyoga), and cognitive attributes like Intellect (buddhi).

definition: Dynamic features inherent in substances that directly cause conjunction or disjunction.
details: Five types of motion: Upward (utkṣepana), Downward (avakṣepana), Contraction (ākuñcana), Expansion (prasāraṇa), and Locomotion/Going (gamana).

definition: The eternal, singular essence common to many individuals.
details: For example, 'cow-ness' (gotva) in all individual cows. Found in substances, qualities, and actions. High-level generality is Existence (sattā).

definition: The eternal category that distinguishes ultimate, indivisible entities from each other.
details: What makes one eternal atom of earth uniquely distinct from another identical atom of earth. Resides exclusively in eternal substances.

definition: An eternal, inseparable, and singular relation connecting entities.
details: For instance, the relation between a whole object and its parts (cloth and threads), a substance and its quality (blue and lotus), or a universal and its individual.

definition: A category representing the negative aspect of reality, added/codified in syncretic Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika.
details: Four types: Prior (prāgabhāva), Posterior/Destructive (pradhvaṃsābhāva), Absolute (atyantābhāva), and Mutual Exclusion (anyonyābhāva).
